recentItems.title: US President Trump to discuss AI with Chinese President Xi | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Top US and Chinese officials have discussed creating a new "notification mechanism" for AI incidents that could affect national security, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters on Sunday.

Bessent made the comments after what he called "successful" talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York.

The meeting came as US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are due to hold a summit in Washington.

AI has come under intense scrutiny in recent days after researchers warned of the potential risks posed by the technology and some of the industry's most high profile figures called for developers to take a more cautious approach.

What did Donald Trump say at the United Nations General Assembly? | BBC News
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has warned Iran it could face "annihilation" without a US deal over the ongoing conflict, although he said he believed an agreement would be made after US mid-term elections in November.
 
Trump said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is a man he can do business with as they met for the first time in New York.
But he criticised the UK's plan to hand sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius - the islands which are home to a joint US-UK military base.
Trump also met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on the sidelines.

recentItems.title: Earl Spencer should pull Diana book from shelves, Piers Morgan says | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Piers Morgan has called for Earl Spencer's book about Princess Diana to be pulled from the shelves over a factual error.
 
Earl Spencer, Princess Diana's brother, apologised to Morgan for incorrectly describing him in the memoir as the editor of the Daily Mirror when the Mirror Group published "highly intrusive photographs of Princess Diana at the gym" in 1993.
 
Speaking to the BBC, Morgan said he accepted the apology but that his lawyers would be "laying out that we want the offending pages to be removed from this book. And if that means they pulp the first edition, so be it".
 
The BBC understands Penguin, the publishers of Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, will be amending this one point in future editions of the book.

recentItems.title: New data shows El Niño is strongest ever with major shift in global weather patterns | BBC News
recentItems.description:
The developing El Niño climate event is now the strongest on record, according to scientists monitoring Pacific Ocean temperatures. 

The powerful natural climate phenomenon pushes up global temperatures and can increase the risks of extreme weather.

Added to the effects of human-induced climate change, the Met Office is warning that it is "very likely" to mean 2027 is the hottest year on record globally.

There is growing evidence that weather patterns around the world are already being affected, with below-average monsoon rains in India and suppressed hurricane activity in the Atlantic Ocean.

There is no clear evidence that climate change is making El Niño events more likely, but its weather impacts are likely to be more extreme in a warming world.

recentItems.title: How have Iran responded to Donald Trump's threat? | BBC News
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has told the United Nations General Assembly he faces a "big decision" on whether to strike Iran again or pursue a peace deal.

A single member of Iran's delegation watched on during the president's speech in New York, in which he said he could "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if the conflict went unresolved.

Trump later told reporters that American officials had had a "very productive" three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the general assembly.

Iran state TV confirmed that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had met US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff, although there was no comment from officials in Tehran.

recentItems.description:
World leaders have descended on New York for this year's UN General Assembly.
 
It's regarded as diplomacy's biggest event of the year, and will be the first time US President Donald Trump meets UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
 
But what is it all about? What do they do? And why does it matter?
